image_description: An underwater close-up shot of a grey whale's head and upper torso. The image highlights the characteristic mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches (callosities). The rostrum is visible, along with one pectoral flipper tucked against the body. The lighting is dim, typical of underwater photography, with particulate matter in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle of the photo shows the side/underbelly of the head; the top of the rostrum and blowholes are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture clearly displays the chaotic mottling and white callosity patches characteristic of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped to the head and shoulders; the posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be is outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior section is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified from this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint; the visible body skin matches the description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or obscured by shadow/angle; baleen plates are internal and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, paddle-shaped flipper is clearly visible on the left side of the frame, consistent with grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: High-resolution details on the snout and flipper show the rough, bumpy texture associated with cyamids and barnacles.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight smudging or 'painterly' blur in the water background near the top left, lacking the natural particulate randomness of real underwater photos, though subtle.
Edges of the flipper blend slightly into the dark water without sharp occlusion boundaries, common in AI generation but also possible in low-light photography.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification that the subject is indeed a grey whale and not another cetacean species (e.g., humpback or right whale) based on skin pattern and head shape.
To check for seamless integration of the flipper with the body and ensure no 'melting' artifacts at the contact points with the water.
To assess if the underwater lighting and particulate effects look physically consistent or if there are global coherence issues.
To verify that the whale sits correctly within the 3D volume of the water and doesn't appear flat or pasted on.

Check the flipper's connection to the body for any subtle fusion artifacts. Since the blowholes are hidden, rely heavily on the visible head shape and skin texture for classification confirmation.
